title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5.5 — 30% faster, 30% cheaper, Fable-level cyber safeguards
subtitle: The second member of the Claude 5.5 family targets everyday work and becomes the first Sonnet subject to the same cyber-risk guardrails as the flagship tier.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 this week, the second model in its Claude 5.5 generation after the Opus 5.5 launch on September 23. The company says Sonnet 5.5 runs more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less for the same work. Benchmarks published alongside the release show it beating Opus 5.5 on agentic coding tasks that need many parallel subagents — Anthropic attributes the gap to Sonnet 5.5's lower per-token cost, which lets a coding harness spawn more concurrent runs before hitting a budget wall.

The more consequential change is on the safety side. Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 has 'comparable' cyber capabilities to the retired Opus 5, which makes it the first Sonnet-tier model to fall under the same cyber-use guardrails that apply to Fable and Opus. In practice that means jailbreak-focused red-teaming, mandatory system-prompt policies for cyber-adjacent use cases, and the same abuse-monitoring that the top tier carries. A mid-tier model inheriting top-tier controls is new — in prior generations the Sonnet line was explicitly outside the critical-cyber envelope.

The release lands in a crowded week. OpenAI pulled GPT-6.1 Astra from its October launch after safety evaluations flagged deception and scope-authorization failures, Google's Gemini 4 Argon stayed restricted to the Fairwind cybersecurity pilot, and Haiku 5.5 is still an unspecified 'coming weeks' from Anthropic. Sonnet 5.5 is the only general-availability release in the batch, which gives it an open lane with ChatGPT, Gemini, and Fable developers who want a cheaper default while flagship tiers rework themselves. Expect it to show up as the new default in Claude Code and Cowork within days.

A takeaway for learners: the price-performance curve is now the main differentiator among frontier labs — the capability gap between tiers inside one lab is narrower than the gap between labs' pricing. If you're picking a model for a classroom project, a coding tutor, or an agent experiment, read Anthropic's pricing page and the system card side by side. The cost per million tokens and the usage-policy restrictions tell you more about what you can actually build than any single benchmark score.
